extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies (HR/personnel offices), agency counsel, Merit Systems Protection Board practitioners, and affected federal employees/employee advocates
extracted.subtask_short: OPM final rule: civil service protections
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule text and accompanying explanation from the Office of Personnel Management clarifying civil service protections, merit system principles, and regulatory procedures for moving positions and employees between competitive and excepted service schedules, and for adverse actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit System Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The CSRA codified fundamental merit system principles summarized as: (1) Recruit, select, and advance on merit after fair and open competition; (2) Treat employees and applicants fairly and equitably; (3) Provide equal pay for equal work and reward excellent performance; (4) Maintain high standards of integrity, conduct, and concern for the public interest; (5) Manage employees efficiently and effectively; (6) Retain or separate employees on the basis of their performance; (7) Educate and train employees if it will result in better organizational or individual performance; (8) Protect employees from improper political influence; (9) Protect employees against reprisal for the lawful disclosure of illegality and other covered wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles form the substantive policy objectives the rule is intended to protect and reinforce; they inform interpretation of regulatory amendments and agency personnel practices described throughout the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'employee' under 5 U.S.C. 7511(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 7511(a), 'employee' includes: (1) competitive service individuals who are not serving a probationary/trial period under an initial appointment or who have completed 1 year of current continuous service under other than a temporary appointment limited to 1 year or less; (2) preference eligibles in the excepted service who have completed 1 year of current continuous service in the same or similar positions in an Executive agency, USPS, or PRC; and (3) excepted service individuals (other than preference eligibles) who are not serving a probationary/trial period pending conversion to the competitive service or who have completed 2 years of current continuous service in the same or similar positions under other than a temporary appointment limited to 2 years or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an individual qualifies as an 'employee' determines entitlements to chapter 75 procedural protections and MSPB appeal rights; agencies and adjudicators must apply these service-duration and probationary criteria when assessing coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories excepted from chapter 75 protections (5 U.S.C. 7511(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories are excepted from chapter 75 protections, including officers appointed by the President with Senate advice and consent, officers the President is permitted to appoint, and individuals 'whose position has been determined to be of a confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations that a position falls within these exceptions remove chapter 75 adverse action protections from incumbents; OPM interprets the 'confidential/policy-' language as intended to except noncareer political appointees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse action appealability and procedural protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspensions of 14 days or less are not directly appealable to the MSPB but entitle the employee to procedural protections (notice, an opportunity to respond, representation, and a written decision). More rigorous procedures and appealability to the MSPB apply before removals, demotions, suspensions for more than 14 days, reductions in grade or pay, and furloughs for 30 days or less for individuals who meet the definition of 'employee' under 5 U.S.C. 7511(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow statutory/regulatory procedural steps appropriate to the type of adverse action; the rule clarifies which actions are appealable and what procedural minima apply for non-appealable short suspensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of accrued civil service protections upon involuntary move
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil servants in the competitive or excepted service who qualify as 'employees' under 5 U.S.C. 7501/7511(a) will retain rights previously accrued upon an involuntary move from the competitive service to the excepted service, or from one excepted service schedule to another, or any subsequent involuntary move, unless the employee relinquishes such rights or status by voluntarily encumbering a position that explicitly results in a loss of, or different, rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies moving positions or employees involuntarily must recognize and preserve accrued adverse action/status rights; voluntary acceptance of a position that explicitly changes rights requires an informed written statement (see notice/acknowledgment requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating' positions
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM interprets these terms of art (applied throughout 5 CFR chapter I, subchapter B) to describe positions generally excepted from chapter 75 protections and reinforces the longstanding view that Congress intended this exception to cover noncareer political appointees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interpretive rule is used to classify positions that are not entitled to chapter 75 protections; agencies must apply the clarified definitions when determining whether positions are properly excepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency procedures when moving individuals or positions (5 CFR part 302 amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM amends part 302 to provide specific procedures when moving individuals or positions from the competitive service to the excepted service, or between excepted service schedules, aiming to add transparency and provide a right of appeal to the MSPB to the extent any such move is involuntary and characterized as stripping individuals of previously accrued status and protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow the new procedural steps set out in part 302 (including notice, scope, basic requirements) and prepare to justify moves that could be characterized as stripping accrued protections; failure to follow the procedures may render the move improper and subject to MSPB relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for moving positions (Part 302—'Procedures for Moving Positions')
rubrics_metrics.description: When moving positions into or within the excepted service, agencies must follow defined procedures in part 302 (e.g., scope, basic requirements) and consider implications such as retention of status and rights; OPM omits Schedules D and E from certain regulatory changes due to their unique statutory/administrative schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should document the basis for moves, consider veterans' preference and other statutory obligations 'as far as administratively feasible,' and account for any special rules applicable to certain schedules (e.g., Pathways, ALJs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice rights for encumbered positions (employee acknowledgement for voluntary moves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 5 CFR 302.102(b), when an employee serving under a temporary appointment in the competitive service is selected for an excepted appointment, the agency must: (1) inform the employee that the position is in the excepted service and that acceptance will take them out of the competitive service while occupying the position; and (2) obtain a written statement from the employee acknowledging they understand they are leaving the competitive service voluntarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written acknowledgement is required for voluntary changes that affect status; agencies must ensure employees are informed of consequences to rights/status before accepting such appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights for encumbered positions (Section 302.603 / MSPB appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies' moves that are involuntary and characterized as stripping individuals of previously accrued civil service status and protections trigger a right of appeal to the Merit Systems Protection Board under the amended part 302 provisions and other applicable regulations (e.g., 5 CFR part 752/75 procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where involuntary actions effectively remove accrued rights, employees may appeal to MSPB; agencies should ensure moves are legally justified and procedurally correct to withstand MSPB review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of chapter 75 vs chapter 43 for performance-based actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an employee's performance is determined to be unacceptable, the agency may respond under chapter 75 (efficiency of the service) or pursue a performance-based action under chapter 43 at the agency's discretion; a mere difference of opinion with leadership does not qualify as misconduct or unacceptable performance warranting adverse action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must select the proper statutory vehicle (chapter 43 for performance-based removals or chapter 75 procedures) and document objective performance deficiencies, since subjective disagreement is insufficient to justify adverse action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming regulatory changes for non-appealable adverse actions (alignment with 5 U.S.C. 7501 and precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule conforms regulations for non-appealable adverse actions to statutory language in 5 U.S.C. 7501 and Federal Circuit precedent to clarify which employees are covered by the non-appealable adverse action provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text now more closely tracks statutory definitions and controlling case law; agencies should review definitions of covered employees when invoking non-appealable adverse actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of probationary period rules for Department of Defense employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule updates regulations to reflect the repeal of 10 U.S.C. 1599e (effective December 31, 2022) and restores a one-year probationary period for covered Department of Defense employees appointed to permanent positions within the competitive service in the Department of Defense on or after December 31, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD HR offices and appointing officials must apply the one-year probationary period for covered appointments made on or after the specified date; this affects when individuals acquire 'employee' status for chapter 75 protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: rule addresses chapter 75 adverse action rights (not prohibited personnel practices/chapter 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM explains this final rule deals with adverse action rights under chapter 75 and corresponding regulations, but it does not address prohibited personnel practices or accrued protections under 5 U.S.C. chapter 23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that implicate prohibited personnel practices (chapter 23) involve distinct processes and are not remedied by the chapter 75-focused regulatory text in this rule; agencies and claimants should pursue the appropriate statutory track for prohibited personnel practice allegations.
